candidates.note: Up to 2 checker assignments per contact (117 check scans). More commits at fixed per-sighting error = more chances for a wrong majority. Even unanimous >=3 admits 1 dangerous commit (23 commits).

Twelve live episodes: eleven cleared at the reconnect tier (fired at ~303-329 s of silence, service back in ~2 s, no restart); one episode associated and regained an IP yet stayed deaf inbound and was ended by an operator reboot — restart tier still unexercised, and a design gap is identified (any single panel success clears escalation, so partial deafness can loop reconnects). Windows between wedges ranged ~15-123 min (not monotonic). Episodes counted from controller serial-log watchdog lines cross-checked with /api/health disconnect counters (2026-11-05); two ~1 min self-clearing transients excluded. Trigger still open.

decision_flow: Host or Korvo planner assigns simulated search routes per unit
Simulation evaluates a tile scan -> sighting with identify roll (accuracy 60-82% by cover)
Lone sighting? -> assign budget-checked independent checker
Checker scans same contact (energy + return-reserve checked)
Commit rule: majority across >=N sightings (v4: asymmetric)
Committed labels scored vs ground truth: recall, mislabels, Enemy->Friendly, energy, landings
Pre-registered gates decide promote/reject before any firmware ships
